task.name: A story is seated with an allocation that cannot fund the review cycles it is permitted, so verification is defunded by arithmetic
task.story_text:
## Observed

A story is seated with an allocation that cannot fund both its own dev estimate and the review
cycles it is permitted, so verification is defunded by arithmetic rather than by any overrun.

Story `issue-2204` was seated with the limits it would run under recorded up front:

```
adaptive limits: dev_max=3 review_max=5 dev_cost_estimate=$25.04
story allocation: $48.02
review pool cost: $17.55 per cycle (3 reviewers, tier strong)
```

Those numbers do not admit the permitted behaviour. A dev estimate of $25.04 against a $48.02
allocation leaves $22.98, which funds one review cycle and a fraction of a second — for a story
explicitly allowed five. The shortfall was determined at seating time, before any work ran.

The story then behaved close to its own estimate: dev consumed $26.43 against $25.04 predicted, a
5% overrun. Review cycle 1 cost $7.81. Review cycle 2 was refused for lack of funds:
`cannot fund its planned review participants — needs $17.55, $12.96 left`, and the story escalated.

The ordering makes the loss specific. Dev runs first and draws from the same pool, so the phases
that consume budget early are funded and the phase that verifies them is what runs out. A story
that needs more dev iterations is a story with more to check, and it is exactly that story which
arrives at review with nothing left to spend.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** a story exhausts its allocation before running a review cycle it was
  permitted, and escalates for want of funds rather than on any finding.
- **Evidence:** run `88a7e2cc81eb`, story `issue-2204`. Seating logged
  `adaptive limits: dev_max=3 review_max=5 dev_cost_estimate=$25.0428` against a $48.02 allocation.
  Review cycle 1 cost $7.81; the attempt at cycle 2 logged `Story allocation exhausted ... needs
  $17.55, $12.96 left of the $48.02 allocation`. Dev totalled $26.43 across three iterations.
- **Ruled out:** not a dev overrun — dev finished within 5% of the estimate computed at seating.
- **Ruled out:** not an unforeseeable review cost — the pool composition and its per-cycle cost are
  known when the panel is seated, from the same complexity signal that set the allocation.
- **Ruled out:** not a quality failure — every gate run passed, and the escalation names funding,
  not a finding.
- **Confirmed cause:** the allocation is sized without reserving for the review cycles the same
  seating decision permits, so the permitted iteration counts and the money available to run them
  are set independently and are not reconciled against each other.
- **Affected code path:** story allocation and adaptive-limit seating, and the review-participant
  funding check that refuses a cycle at dispatch.
- **Fix-success criterion:** a story is not seated with permissions it cannot afford to exercise —
  either the allocation covers the phases it authorises, or the authorisation is reduced to what the
  allocation covers, and the operator can see which happened.

## Expected

A budget and the permissions it funds should be decided together. Granting a story five review
cycles while allocating enough for one is not a limit, it is a limit that will be discovered as a
failure partway through, after money has been spent on work that cannot then be checked.

Where the two cannot both be honoured, the system should reconcile them at the point it still has a
choice — before dispatch, where reducing scope is free — rather than at the point where the only
remaining options are to escalate or to accept unverified work. Verification failing for lack of
funds is worse than any other phase failing that way, because it is the phase whose absence is
hardest to detect afterwards: the work looks finished, and nothing recorded says it was never
checked.

handoff.summary: Adds a deterministic seating-time reconciliation between a story's allocation and the review cycles it is permitted. reconcile_review_cycles() in story_budget.py is pure arithmetic over the allocation, spend already incurred (preflight/plan/plan-review, via state.total_cost_measured), the adaptive dev cost estimate, and the per-cycle review-pool cost (sum of configured review_pool budget_usd — the same upper-bound number the dispatch-time guard plans against). _coordinator_loop applies it immediately after derive_limits(), before state.adaptive_review_max is read by any dispatch: it lowers review_max to the affordable count, or refuses at seating (Phase.ESCALATE, error_type=allocation_exhausted, via seating_shortfall() which reuses the existing phase_funding_shortfall payload shape so every consumer reads it unchanged) when not even one cycle fits. Only a band-derived allocation governs — the configured fallback is by construction one pass through every role, so reconciling against it would clamp verification to a single cycle on every project without band history; that plus absent allocation, absent dev estimate, zero pool cost and cost-unknown spend are explicit recorded no-ops. The dispatch-time guard in review_pool.py is untouched. Full decision lands in the adaptive_limits audit block and rationale line.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A story is not seated with permissions it cannot afford to exercise — either the allocation covers the phases it authorises, or the authorisation is reduced to what the allocation covers, and the operator can see which happened.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Reconciliation runs in _coordinator_loop right after derive_limits() and before any dev/review dispatch. Reduced case: adaptive_review_max is lowered to the affordable count (seam test asserts the reduced value is in force at the dev call site, not after). Unfundable case (not one cycle affordable): the run escalates before DEV rather than clamping review_max to 0, because 0 is read as 'unset' by three call sites that fall back to config.retry.max_review_cycles. Operator visibility: review_cycle_reconciliation dict (requested vs reconciled review_max, allocation_usd, spent_so_far_usd, dev_cost_estimate_usd, review_cycle_cost_usd, affordable_review_cycles, remaining_after_dev_usd, shortfall_usd, basis, action) is written into state.adaptive_limits_audit, which audit.py:758 carries into the run audit; the reduction is also appended to the adaptive-limits rationale line and logged. Scoped to substrate-derived allocations — see story_deviations.

story_deviations: Reconciliation is gated on allocation basis == substrate_band. Applying it to configured_fallback allocations regressed 8 existing coordinator integration tests, because _configured_story_budget() defines the fallback as one pass through every role — it therefore funds exactly one review cycle by construction, independent of the story, and would clamp review_max to 1 on every project without band history. The spec's evidence case (issue-2204, $48.02 from band percentiles) is substrate-derived and still reconciles. The pre-existing dispatch-time guard continues to cover fallback allocations against measured spend.

Plan Step 3 named audit_render.py; it does not render adaptive_limits today, so no change was made there. audit.py:758 already carries state.adaptive_limits_audit into the run audit and a seam test asserts the reconciliation block arrives via generate_audit_log().

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 does not say what happens when the allocation cannot fund even ONE review cycle (affordable == 0). Clamping review_max to 0 would silently seat a story whose work is never checked — precisely the outcome the spec calls hardest to detect afterwards ('the work looks finished, and nothing recorded says it was never checked').
  Suggestion: Treat affordable == 0 as a distinct outcome from a downward clamp: refuse at seating (escalate before dev spends) rather than reducing review_max to 0, and record that action explicitly in the Step 3 audit fields.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's per-cycle cost input is unspecified for the cases where it cannot be computed honestly: state.story_allocation may be absent, and total_cost_measured may be unmeasured (review_pool.py:620 already skips its own check on both grounds — if enforce_budgets and state.story_allocation, and the 'lower bound is not a number to refuse work on' comment).
  Suggestion: Make the reconciler a no-op that records why it declined when allocation is absent, spend is unmeasured, or the pool cost is zero — reducing a permission on a guessed number is worse than leaving the dispatch-time guard to catch it.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 says 'the same review pool data that later feeds the review funding check', but the dispatch check at review_pool.py:621-626 plans against the post-demotion pool, which does not exist at seating time.
  Suggestion: Use sum(float(p.budget_usd) for p in config.review_pool) — verified real (ForgeConfig.review_pool is list[ModelProfile], models.py:130 budget_usd) and an upper bound, since demotion only removes reviewers.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5 lists Files: tests with no target module, and Step 3 lists audit_render.py without naming what it renders today.
  Suggestion: Point the tests at the existing coordinator seam suites and confirm audit_render.py actually renders the adaptive_limits block before editing it; audit.py:758 already carries the dict, so an audit_render change may be unnecessary.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 1/2’s reconciliation arithmetic only reserves dev_cost_estimate_usd; it does not account for spend already incurred before _coordinator_loop runs. In this codebase, PLAN and PLAN_REVIEW happen before _coordinator_loop (src/theforge/coordinator/plan_flow.py, src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py), and the dispatch-time refusal in src/theforge/coordinator/review_pool.py checks against state.total_cost_measured. A story can therefore still be granted review cycles that are unaffordable after preflight/plan spend, so the same funding failure can still occur at review dispatch.
  Suggestion: Include already-incurred story spend in the seating-time reconciliation input and audit record, or move reconciliation to a point that truly runs before any chargeable phase spend.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 1 says to lower adaptive_review_max to the affordable count, but does not handle the 0-cycle case. In the current runtime, state.adaptive_review_max is read with ... or config.retry.max_review_cycles in src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py, src/theforge/coordinator/validate_phase.py, and src/theforge/coordinator/review_phase.py, so 0 is treated as 'unset' and falls back to the configured cap. That means an unfundable story would still proceed until the later funding guard trips.
  Suggestion: Specify a distinct unfundable path: escalate before DEV when fewer than one review cycle is affordable, or change all cap readers to honor an explicit zero-cycle authorization.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
